The proposed amendment requests approval of a high-density mixed-use development consisting of a six-storey low-rise apartment building with approximately 142 units, and a 27-storey market and non-market mixed-use tower with approximately 276 residential units, inclusive of a two-storey commercial podium fronting Kingsway. agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby fee bylaw amendments up for approval, effective Jan 1, 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider further amendments to the Burnaby Consolidated Fees and Charges Bylaw. This bylaw is the City's master list of fees it charges for permits, licences, and services. If approved, the changes would take effect on January 1, 2027. The agenda does not list which specific fees would change, so owners should check the attached proposed amendments to see if their permit or licence fees are affected.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the proposed bylaw amendments to see if your permit or licence fees change, and budget for the new rates starting January 1, 2027.

key_dates.label: Burnaby fee bylaw amendments take effect

agenda_briefs.title: Council to vote on temporary permit for parking facility at 7749 Kingsway
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider Temporary Use Permit #26-07 at its November 24, 2026 meeting. The permit would allow a parking facility at 7749 Kingsway. A Temporary Use Permit is a short-term approval that lets a property be used for something the current zoning rules don't normally allow. If approved, the parking use would be allowed only for the time period and conditions set out in the permit. Council has not yet made a decision.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check the November 24 council agenda and attend if you want to comment on the proposed parking facility at 7749 Kingsway.

key_dates.label: Burnaby Council considers TUP #26-07 parking facility at 7749 Kingsway

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider $500 grant to Tsleil-Waututh Nation Christmas Hamper and Toy Drive
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request to approve a $500 grant to the Tsleil-Waututh Nation Christmas Hamper and Toy Drive. The Nation sent a fundraising appeal letter asking the City for support. If approved, the City would give $500 toward holiday hampers and toys for families. This is a small community grant item on the agenda — it does not propose any new rules, fees, or licence changes for local businesses.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider appointing acting mayors for 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider appointing its councillors to serve as Acting Mayor for 2027. An Acting Mayor is a councillor who fills in for the Mayor when the Mayor is away or unavailable. This is a routine housekeeping item on the agenda. It does not propose any new rules or fees for businesses. It only decides who steps in when the Mayor is absent.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider 2027 meeting schedules and member appointments
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a report that sets the 2027 meeting dates for Council, Public Hearings, and Advisory Bodies and Boards. The same report would appoint Council members to regional and local organizations, Standing Committees, and legislated Advisory Bodies. This is a procedural item — it decides when Council meets and who sits on which bodies next year, not a new rule for businesses. The outcome could affect when public hearings happen in 2027, which matters if you plan to speak on a development or licence application.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check the approved 2027 meeting schedule once it is posted so you know when public hearings will be held.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposed bylaw (No. 14839) that would change an earlier rezoning at 7211 Greenford Ave. The original plan, approved in December 2024, allowed a six-storey rental building and a 41-storey strata tower. The new proposal would replace that with a six-storey apartment building of about 142 units and a 27-storey mixed-use tower of about 276 residential units, plus a two-storey commercial base along Kingsway. A final adoption memo is scheduled for November 24, 2026.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider amending Burnaby's 2026–2030 Financial Plan
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider Bylaw #14857, which would amend the city's 2026–2030 Consolidated Five-Year Financial Plan. The change comes from an administrative report presented to Council on October 27, 2026. If approved, the amendment would update the city's spending and revenue plans for the next five years. The bylaw is still a proposal and has not been passed. Business owners should watch for details on how the change could affect municipal fees, taxes, or services.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on Bylaw #14857 — it could affect future municipal fees or taxes.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Sidley Street residents' petition on proposed rezoning REZ #26-07
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a petition from Sidley Street residents about a proposed rezoning (REZ #26-07) of 5168, 5180 and 5192 Sidley Street. A rezoning is a change to the rules for what can be built or done on a property. The petition documents are on the agenda for the meeting on November 24, 2026. Council has not yet made a decision on the rezoning, and the petition shows neighbours have concerns about the proposal. Owners near the site should watch what Council decides, since a rezoning can change what gets built nearby.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check the November 24, 2026 council agenda and attend if you want to speak about the proposed Sidley Street rezoning.
